title: The general confession (1662)
hookLine: we have left undone those things which we ought to have done
tomorrow: how many things can one thank-you note hold?

cards: The obvious place to start an apology is the thing done: the words said, the door slammed. The Book of Common Prayer of 1662 starts somewhere else.

Its general confession, meant for everyone in church to say at once, puts this first: "We have left undone those things which we ought to have done." The call that never got made. The question nobody asked.
Only after that come the things done.

teach.b: It's called general because nobody says it alone: the whole congregation says it together, after the minister, kneeling.
It opens with a picture: "We have erred, and strayed from thy ways like lost sheep." Sheep don't storm off; they wander, one mouthful at a time.
Then the two halves, undone and done, and a hard line after them: "And there is no health in us." Then a turn in the grammar. "Spare thou them, O God, which confess their faults."
The people have been saying we and us; now they step back and speak of themselves as them, the ones who confess. There's no list of particular sins.
Each person brings their own, silently, inside the shared words.
Look back over the week and it fits: the Imitation wanted the sorrow, not the definition; Luther gave thanks before asking; the free servant kept no score.
Today the prayer book adds the honest list, with the undone things first.

how: In the 1662 Book of Common Prayer, the general confession is said by the whole congregation at Morning and Evening Prayer; Anglican and Episcopal churches still use it or later forms of it.

a list of sins the minister reads out for everyone

games.q: the general confession — tap the pairs.

s: a confession means listing the bad things you did
the likely assumption. this one starts with what was left undone, and names no particular sins.
in the 1662 prayer book, the whole congregation says it together
the prayer pictures people as rebels storming away from God
it says we have erred and strayed like lost sheep.

games.q: your team lost, and the captain asks for a list of mistakes. one player says, 'I didn't do anything wrong.' what would the general confession add?
o: then she has nothing to confess this time.
what we left undone counts too, and goes first.
only the coach should list the mistakes.
games.why: the confession says we have left undone those things which we ought to have done, before it names the things done.

practice: Close your eyes and let one undone thing come to mind, something small you meant to do and didn't. Don't argue with it or explain it away; just name it honestly.
If you pray, you can bring it with the prayer book's own line: spare thou them, O God, which confess their faults.

wordCard.voice: The general confession. The prayer book's confession for the whole congregation, said together, with each person's own faults held silently inside it.

carryVoice: Your line: spare thou them. The undone things go first on the list. Week done.
